doc.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18

title: Mazurkas and the very fast waltz
summary: They discuss how mazurkas, a fast waltz, were played in time. Williams says they are counted in one and recalls playing one in the old WPA band.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Remember how they would play the mazookas? How would they play in time again? I remember playing that around here.
I know it about music. I never played that around.
It was a fast waltz. I never did hear one in my life.

Except on violin and classical pieces. They don't play any dances here anymore. No, they don't play. We played like a kid. We used to call it the one, but there's a very fast waltz tempo. You're counting three, but it's most likely in one. You see, it's a... Last time I was playing a part of something, I think it was something we had in the old WPA band. It was very fast. It was the main guys that was living there. His bass drum is hitting... You wouldn't want to tackle that, no. No, no, I don't. No, that's the thing. I never used that. No, I guess not. Waltzes are the main thing. Do you have a practice pad?
